subject: reasoning
question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). B sits third to the right of E. E sits second to the left of G. G is to the immediate right of F. G is not an immediate neighbour of E. A sits on the immediate right of B and C sits on the immediate left of E. How many people sit between D and B when counted from the left of D?
solution:
A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order).

 
• B sits third to the right of E.
 
• E sits second to the left of G.
 
• G is to the immediate right of F.
 
• G is not an immediate neighbour of E.
 
• A sits on the immediate right of B and C sits on the immediate left of E

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf1618ca5f7fadde80a54f71ff6034575fb2ef3064e6e6684607d500a5ae1c60.png] 

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**
